dietEvidence.body: The skull and dentition indicate herbivory. No gut contents are known; the plants eaten and the feeding height are inferred from anatomy.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A large sauropod with a relatively simple vertebral column and a short neck for its body size. Its relationships among early sauropods are debated.
summary: A large sauropod with a relatively simple vertebral column and a short neck for its body size. Its relationships among early sauropods are debated.

discovery.body: Named by Sereno et al., 1999. The record is known from the Tiourarén Formation, Niger. The holotype, MNN TIG3, is a largely complete skeleton; several individuals, including a juvenile, were found at the same locality.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: The holotype, MNN TIG3, is a largely complete skeleton. Several individuals, including a juvenile with possible tooth marks, were found at the same locality.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Tiourarén Formation, Niger records the species in the Middle Jurassic. The numeric range used here is ≈167–161 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The skull and most of the postcranium are known. The vertebral column is relatively simple for a sauropod, and the neck is short relative to the body.

behaviour.body: Several individuals, including a juvenile, occur at one site. That is a mass-death assemblage; gregarious behaviour is an inference from the association, not an observed fact.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from a partial skeleton and referred material from Niger. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The holotype, MNN TIG3, is a largely complete skeleton including the skull and most of the postcranium. Several individuals, including a juvenile, were found at the same locality. The Tiourarén Formation is now read as Middle Jurassic, not Early Cretaceous as in the original description.

primer.lead: Jobaria tiguidensis was a large sauropod from the [Middle Jurassic](/deep-time?period=jurassic) of Niger. It had a relatively short neck for a sauropod and a vertebral column that is simpler than those of many later giants.
paragraphs: The holotype, MNN TIG3, is a largely complete skeleton including the skull and most of the postcranium. Several individuals, including a juvenile, were found at the same site. The Tiourarén Formation was originally thought to be Early Cretaceous, but later work supports a Middle Jurassic age.

The mass-death assemblage is direct evidence that several animals were buried together; gregarious behaviour is an inference. Its plant diet is inferred from the skull and teeth, and no gut contents are known.
primer.takeaway: A short-necked sauropod from a Middle Jurassic mass-death site.
